title: Beta Training
subtitle: Training faster activity associated with active processing
altText: Chalkboard-style clinical diagram illustrating beta training within a neurofeedback closed loop.
learningObjectives: Explain beta training without diagnostic overreach.
Distinguish measurement, mechanism and clinical outcome in beta training.
Identify one safety or validity limitation relevant to beta training.

sections.explainSimply: Beta protocols generally reinforce activity above alpha frequencies, but exact bands and goals vary.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Beta can reflect cortical activation, sensorimotor processing or muscle artifact. High-beta metrics are particularly vulnerable to EMG contamination.
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Monitor tension, headache, agitation, sleep and arousal. Claims of band-specific symptom effects require controlled evidence.
sections.thinkOfItLike: Choosing a camera lens: every method emphasises some information and introduces its own distortions.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Psychologists need to understand beta training to evaluate mechanism claims, informed consent, treatment fit and whether change transfers to real-world function.
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Forehead or jaw muscle can masquerade as increased beta.
sections.clinicalPearl: The trained metric is an intermediate target; the clinical endpoint is meaningful function.
sections.practicalExample: A clinician using beta training predefines the target, checks raw signal and artifacts, monitors symptoms and function, and reviews whether change generalises beyond the feedback display.
sections.limitationsCautions: Forehead or jaw muscle can masquerade as increased beta. Evidence classification: protocol-specific; mixed evidence.
